styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Golden-domed monasteries, WWII sites and Soviet relics.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Opera, folk art and the wide river boulevards.

stays.why: Central and walkable to Maidan, Khreshchatyk and the metro; easiest base for a first visit.
Old riverside quarter with cafés and bars; quieter streets, still close to the centre.
Near the Pechersk Lavra and museum district; leafy and calm, good for history lovers.
Upscale government quarter beside the centre; quiet, safe-feeling and close to Khreshchatyk.

food: Try borscht (beet soup with sour cream), varenyky (filled dumplings) and chicken Kyiv; portions are big and prices low.
Cheap eats: cafeteria-style 'stolova' places and bakery cafés serve a full lunch for a few hundred грн.
Book a table for dinner on weekends in Podil; popular spots fill up.
Drink local: try uzvar (dried-fruit drink) and honey-based drinks; coffee culture is strong, with many small roasters.
Check opening hours on the day; some places change hours at short notice.
more_time: Add a half-day at the Pechersk Lavra and the nearby WWII museum if you like history.
Swap one city day for a river walk and the Kyiv Sea embankment on a warm day.
Art lovers can spend an afternoon at the PinchukArtCentre and the folk-art museum.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Lavra, Maidan and Podil at an easy pace; add a night for museums and the river.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 0°C, lows around -5°C; pack a warm coat and expect about 11 wet days.
February: still cold, highs near 2°C; short days, so plan indoor sights.
March: warming to about 7°C; mix of sun and rain, about 9 wet days.
April: mild at 15°C; good for walking, but keep a rain layer for about 10 wet days.
May: pleasant at 20°C; one of the best months for parks and the river.
June: warm at 26°C; long evenings, about 10 wet days.
July: hot at 26°C with lows near 17°C; the busiest month, book ahead.
August: hottest, highs near 27°C; go out early and rest at midday.
September: comfortable at 21°C; fewer wet days, about 7.
October: cooler at 13°C; about 8 wet days, bring layers.
November: chilly at 6°C; about 10 wet days, short daylight.
December: cold at 2°C with lows near -2°C; the wettest month, about 13 wet days.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate: cold winters, warm summers and rain spread across the year.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Warm days around 20–27°C and long evenings. Ideal for walking and the river.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs near 0–2°C and lows to -5°C. Pack a heavy coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 6–13 wet days each month; December is wettest. Carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Big swings
items.text: Days can warm up then cool fast in spring and autumn; dress in layers.

items.title: Golden autumn
items.text: September and October are mild and colourful, with fewer wet days than summer.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for hilly streets; warm gear in winter.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; ride apps for late nights and hills.

modes.text: Fast and cheap; base fare is 8 грн per trip. Pay by tapping a contactless card or phone at orange gates.
Trams, trolleybuses and buses share the same 8 грн fare; transfers cost extra.
Bolt and Uber work well; Uklon is the local favourite. Curfew is 01:00-05:00 daily, so plan your ride home early.
Not needed in the centre; traffic and parking are a hassle. Use metro and apps instead.
Central streets are walkable but hilly; underground crossings have stairs, not lifts.
